title: Ops Helm: procedural fragments catalog and staged execution shim
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a curated catalog of small, composable procedural fragments (shelllets) that can be composed into support playflows and executed with staged safety gates. Deliver a lightweight shim that taskifies these fragments, exposes a typed invocation API, and integrates with existing admin RBAC and telemetry so first-line engineers can run safe, auditable remediation steps without full runbook orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog prototype with at least 12 vetted fragments covering common high-frequency support actions (e.g., rotate-service-key, cache-invalidate, restart-worker, collect-diagnostics).
Shim exposes an HTTP API and CLI that accepts typed params and returns structured status/diagnostics within 2s for noop and 10s for typical blocking steps.
Execution path includes pre-flight policy checks (RBAC, cooldown, maintenance window) and a two-step approval for destructive fragments.
All executions emit unified telemetry (trace id, tokens consumed, wall time, outcome) to the ops dashboard and a dedicated BigQuery table.
Security review completed and KMS-integrated for credentialed fragments.
notes: 2026-02-25: Kickoff — scoped MVP to catalog + shim; prioritized safety and auditability after recent pager incident.
2026-03-01: Spike done — prototyped fragment contract (name, schema, run, dry-run). Found two common failure modes: idempotency gaps and flaky network calls.
2026-03-04: Design sync with PM/Support — agreed on typed params + OpenAPI spec; decided to reuse existing RBAC library rather than ship new auth code to reduce audit surface.
2026-03-07: Implemented dry-run and dry-validate modes; initial telemetry events wired to dev-cluster dashboard.
2026-03-11: Security review request submitted; noted requirement for KMS-wrapped secrets for any fragment that uses credentials.
review_feedback: PM (R. Alvarez): prefer smaller fragments that are single-responsibility to make approvals simpler.
Design (L. Chen): suggest a simple confirmation UI for the console that surfaces the typed params and estimated impact before run.
SRE (T. O'Connor): flagged heavy reliance on network calls — recommend circuit-breaker and retries with jitter in the runtime shim.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): define fragment schema, implement 12 fragments, build shim HTTP API + CLI, wire dry-run + telemetry.
Phase 2: add staged approvals, two-step destructive confirmations, and KMS secret access.
Phase 3: console integration with confirmation UI, RBAC policy granularities, and rollout to staging/dedicated clusters.
Phase 4: bake into incident responder flows and integrate with runbook-as-task orchestration for multi-step recipes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fragment contracts and idempotency checks.
E2E in staging that runs each fragment with a mocked target and asserts audit events.
Chaos test: simulate partial network failures to exercise circuit-breaker and retry logic.
Security test: validate KMS-wrapped secret retrieval and access denial for unauthorized principals.
rollback_plan: Disable HTTP endpoint via feature flag; execute emergency revocation of fragment registry entries and invalidate short-lived tokens. Postmortem and migration back to scripted runbooks if needed.
decisions: Use typed fragment schema (JSON schema) instead of freeform arguments to reduce operator errors.
Leverage existing RBAC service rather than duplicating auth logic to speed audit sign-off.
Implement dry-run first for every fragment; destructive fragments require explicit two-step confirmation.
next_steps: Complete KMS integration spike (ENG-746210) — blocker for credentialed fragments.
Finish wiring telemetry to BigQuery table and add dashboard tiles for run success/failure rates.
Draft console confirmation UI mockups and get design sign-off (blocking for Phase 3).
